title: Leveraging an Informatics Approach to Identify an Unmet Clinical Need for BRCA1/2 Testing Among Patients With Ovarian Cancer.
authors: Gray, Stacy W; Ottesen, Rebecca A; Currey, Madeline; Cristea, Mihaela; Nikowitz, Janet; Shehayeb, Susan; Lozano, Vanessa; Hom, Julie; Kilburn, Julie; Lopez, Lisa N; Wing, Sam; Sosa, Ernesto; Shen, Jenny; Morris, Michael; Dilsizian, Bedros; Joseph, Thomas; Shen, James; Adeimy, Camille; Phillips, Tanyanika; Bahadini, Bahareh; Niland, Joyce C
one_liner_zh: 该文用NLP从电子病历中评估卵巢癌患者BRCA1/2检测利用率，属临床信息学应用，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: PURPOSE: Although BRCA1/2 testing in ovarian cancer improves outcomes, it is vastly underutilized. Scalable approaches are urgently needed to improve genomically guided care. METHODS: We developed a Natural Language Processing (NLP) pipeline to extract electronic medical record information to identify recipients of BRCA testing. We applied the NLP pipeline to assess testing status in 308 patients with ovarian cancer receiving care at a National Cancer Institute Comprehensive Cancer Center (main campus [MC] and five affiliated clinical network sites [CNS]) from 2017 to 2019. We compared characteristics between (1) patients who had/had not received testing and (2) testing utilization by site. RESULTS: We found high uptake of BRCA testing (approximately 78%) from 2017 to 2019 with no significant differences between the MC and CNS. We observed an increase in testing over time (67%-85%), higher uptake of testing among younger patients (mean age tested = 61 years v untested = 65 years, P = .01), and higher testing among Hispanic (84%) compared with White, Non-Hispanic (78%), and Asian (75%) patients (P = .006). Documentation of referral for an internal genetics consultation for BRCA pathogenic variant carriers was higher at the MC compared with the CNS (94% v 31%). CONCLUSION: We were able to successfully use a novel NLP pipeline to assess use of BRCA testing among patients with ovarian cancer. Despite relatively high levels of BRCA testing at our institution, 22% of patients had no documentation of genetic testing and documentation of referral to genetics among BRCA carriers in the CNS was low. Given success of the NLP pipeline, such an informatics-based approach holds promise as a scalable solution to identify gaps in genetic testing to ensure optimal treatment interventions in a timely manner.
abstract_zh: 目的：尽管BRCA1/2检测在卵巢癌中可改善预后，但其应用严重不足。亟需可扩展的方法来改善基因组指导下的护理。方法：我们开发了一种自然语言处理（NLP）流程，用于提取电子病历信息以识别接受BRCA检测的患者。我们应用该NLP流程评估了2017年至2019年间在国家癌症研究所综合癌症中心（主校区[MC]及五个附属临床网络站点[CNS]）接受护理的308例卵巢癌患者的检测状态。我们比较了（1）已接受与未接受检测患者之间的特征，以及（2）各站点的检测利用率。结果：我们发现2017年至2019年间BRCA检测的接受率较高（约78%），MC与CNS之间无显著差异。我们观察到检测率随时间增加（67%-85%），年轻患者中检测接受率更高（检测者平均年龄=61岁，未检测者=65岁，P = .01），且西班牙裔患者（84%）的检测率高于白人非西班牙裔（78%）和亚裔（75%）患者（P = .006）。MC中BRCA致病性变异携带者转诊至内部遗传咨询的记录率高于CNS（94%对31%）。结论：我们成功使用一种新型NLP流程评估了卵巢癌患者中BRCA检测的使用情况。尽管我们机构中BRCA检测水平相对较高，但22%的患者没有基因检测记录，且CNS中BRCA携带者转诊至遗传咨询的记录率较低。鉴于NLP流程的成功，这种基于信息学的方法有望成为识别基因检测缺口、确保及时实施最佳治疗干预的可扩展解决方案。
